title: 39 Senators Demand ICE Vetting Overhaul and Body Cameras After Houston and Maine Killings
excerpt: Thirty-eight Democratic senators and Independent Sen. Angus King of Maine sent a letter to DHS demanding answers on ICE's vetting of new hires, vehicle pursuit policies, and an immediate body camera rollout — citing the fatal shootings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston and Johan Durán Guerrero in Maine.
content:
On July 20, 2026, a bipartisan coalition of 39 U.S. senators sent a letter to the Department of Homeland Security demanding immediate accountability reforms at ICE following two fatal shootings in Houston (July 7) and Biddeford, Maine (July 13).

  • The letter was led by Maine Independent Sen. Angus King and signed by 38 Democratic senators.
  • Senators demanded transparency about whether ICE reviews family court records, including domestic violence history, when vetting new recruits — directly referencing the Brouillette revelations.
  • The letter demanded swift body camera deployment for all ICE officers, noting that neither the Houston nor the Maine shooting was recorded.
  • Senators asked ICE to require agents to wear uniforms clearly identifying them as "ICE" rather than generic "POLICE" markings.
  • The letter called for clearer standards governing vehicle pursuit and traffic stop procedures.

The senators wrote that "by no stretch could either of the victims in Texas and Maine be characterized as 'the worst of the worst,' making these tragic deaths even more egregious" — pointing to documented failures in hiring standards as a root cause of the incidents.
source: Philadelphia Inquirer / PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
